o.text: Borrowed from Arabic سُكَان (sukān), from Middle Persian, from Akkadian 𒄑𒍣𒃶 (sikkānu, “oar, steering paddle, rudder blade”), from Sumerian 𒄑𒍣𒃶 (zigan, “oar, steering paddle, rudder blade”).
From bəstə + -kar. Compare Turkish bestekâr, Uzbek bastakor.
Inherited from Early Old Oghuz يَنْكَجْ (yengeç), of unclear ultimate origin. Folk etymology derives it from yan (“side”) + -gəc, referring to the sideways walking of crabs.
